_description: Delivery groups for the shared protocols in sync-inline-versions.md. Each canonical base tag belongs to exactly one group and carries a one-line summary and a when line, the text of a skill's guide line. node .claude/scripts/build-protocol-projection.cjs reads this file and writes .claude/skills/shared/protocols/<tag>.md plus protocols/index.json; --check fails when the projection is stale. A tag with no group, a group entry naming a tag the canonical file does not define, or a tag in two groups fails the build. universal is the hook-delivered bundle: its bins entry lists the ordered tags of each delivery message, and no skill or agent carries a universal tag. inlineSkills is empty: all skill entrypoints, including review-family skills, use protocol guides with full-text delivery and a required published-file fallback. A future full-body exception requires an explicit owner decision; guide mode never converts a listed exception and hooks never repeat its carried body. Agents, mode-reference SYNC carriers and fresh reviewer prompts retain their full protocol bodies. A tag entry may name a trigger ("trigger": "<name>") defined under deliveryTriggers: the protocol hooks then deliver the full text only when the trigger applies to the load (a skill listed in the trigger skills, a pattern match in the event text or the session prompts, a pathPattern match in the recent transcript), and the skill guide line stays the path otherwise; an unknown trigger name or an unusable pattern delivers unconditionally. A summary must not contain a semicolon, and neither line may contain the arrow character or a line break, because the guide line is '- `tag` — summary; when → path'.

universal.description: The universal bundle: the framework rules every task follows. No skill, agent, root instruction file or mirror carries it; the universal hook delivers it on the first prompt of a session, again after about 150K tokens of growth or a compaction, and at every sub-agent start. bins is the authored delivery layout: one entry per hook process, each the ordered tags of one message; the build fails when a bin overflows binChars, a tag is missing or a tag is listed twice.
